findings.where: Apostrophes across the page: the article specimen's display title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', the type pair's 'Mark's voice…', and the first screen's photo caption 'Placeholder: Mark's photo…' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: These use straight typewriter apostrophes. The article body, the article's photo caption ('Mark’s photo') and the footer note ('Mark’s own sentence') use curly ones. The straight mark is most visible in the article title, where it is set at display size.
findings.who_objects: Mark, a lawyer who writes carefully, and the development-bank readers judging him on his attention to detail. Two kinds of apostrophe on one page, one of them in a large headline, looks like copy pasted in without proofreading.

findings.where: Palette, the text-pair table, the Ratio column (phone)
findings.fault: The ratio '11.66 : 1' breaks across two lines, leaving '11.66 :' on one line and '1' on the next. The other ratios stay whole, so one figure in the column is broken apart.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the palette on a phone. A ratio split across lines reads as a typesetting slip in a table that exists to show care with numbers.

findings.where: Article specimen, the download row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The title and its 'Lecture · date' line start a few pixels in from the column's left edge. The rules above and below the row, the body text, the list and the subhead all start on the edge itself, so the row looks slightly off the column.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the founder, who will reuse this row as the pattern for every PDF in the list. A small inset that matches nothing else gets copied into every row and reads as a mistake.

findings.where: Footer lockup (the MMM Infra mark with 'Mark M. Moseley · Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com') compared with the header lockup on the first screen (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The header leads with his name in large Newsreader and puts a small mark beside it. The footer turns this around: the mark is several times larger than the header's and comes first, and his name follows in small grey Public Sans, the same as the address. The same lockup gets two opposite treatments.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief says 'his name leads, with the logo beside it'. In the footer the firm's mark becomes the largest element again, and the name is set like a caption.

findings.where: Palette section: the note under the text-pair table and Mist's swatch label, against the header mark on the first screen
findings.fault: The note says that on the first screen 'the mark and the wordmark reverse to warm white'. Mist's label lists only 'second text on slate'. The rendered header mark is in mist, not warm white, so the palette names the wrong colour for the mark.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, who are asked to approve this palette, including which colour the logo takes on the dark ground. The record contradicts what they see.

findings.where: The two buttons: the first screen's 'Write to me directly' action and the motion sketch's 'Replay the opening'
findings.fault: The first-screen action is a block with square corners. The replay button has rounded corners. They are the page's only two buttons, and their corners don't match.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who will judge this tile as a system for later pages. The corner treatment of a button is undecided between two values, and a later page will have to pick one.
